bat-removal.intro: Bat work in Blacksburg concentrates in the older homes along and behind the town's main streets — the early-1900s houses with tall roof voids, layered gables, and fascia that has been patched across a century. Little brown and big brown bats work the Broad River corridor east of town and the creek branches through it, feeding over the water at dusk and returning to the warmest attic gaps they can find, and a Blacksburg attic that sits undisturbed above a quiet house is exactly the maternity roost a colony is selecting for. The staining at the gable peaks and the guano pattern below them usually tell the story years before the homeowners hear a sound.
bat-removal.extendedBody:
Reading a Blacksburg attic colony

Exclusion here starts with the map, not the ladder. Older Blacksburg homes present several candidate entries — gable vents with failed screens, fascia joints opened a quarter-inch by age, the junctions where porch roofs meet the original walls — and a colony uses two or three of them in rotation. We identify the active exits by the staining and the evening flight, then stage the exclusion for the right window: South Carolina has no statute fixing bat dates, and SCDNR's guidance is to avoid sealing while pups are flightless, so a colony found in early summer is mapped and scheduled rather than rushed. When the timing is right, one-way devices go on the active entries and every secondary gap is sealed in the same job — a partial seal on a layered Blacksburg roofline just moves the colony to its second door. No permit is needed for bat work in this state, and any bat found inside the living space is a same-day call, handled carefully and reported through SC DPH if it has had contact with people or pets.

faqs.q: We found a bat inside our Blacksburg house. What should we do?
faqs.a: Close the room off if you can do it safely, keep people and pets out of it, and call us the same day. A single indoor bat is handled immediately, whatever the season — that is different work from an attic exclusion. If the bat had any contact with a person or a pet, or was found in a room where someone was sleeping, tell us when you call: rabies-suspect bats are a public-health matter in South Carolina and go through SC DPH reporting, and we will walk you through exactly what happens next.

faqs.q: How much does bat removal cost in Blacksburg?
faqs.a: It depends on the colony and the roofline — a single-entry colony on a simple gable is one job; a maternity colony using three entries across a layered older roof is another. We inspect first, map every entry, and quote the complete exclusion firmly before work starts, including the sealing of the secondary gaps, because quoting only the main entry is how bat jobs get sold twice. If the colony is found while pups are flightless, the inspection and mapping happen now and the exclusion is scheduled for the right window at the same quoted price.

skunk-removal.intro: Skunk work in Blacksburg is porch-and-outbuilding work. The town's older homes sit on pier foundations with open crawlspace edges, the porches are low and unskirted, and most properties carry a barn, a shed, or a well house within a skunk's nightly walk of the back door. Striped skunks den under those structures through the winter, raise their kits under them in spring, and dig the sandy yards for grubs the rest of the year. The Broad River bottoms east of town and the creek branches keep the population supplied, and the properties on the town's rural edges meet them first.
skunk-removal.extendedBody:
Closing the Blacksburg porch void

Removing the skunk is the first half of a Blacksburg job; the second half is the void it came from. An open under-porch space or an unsealed crawlspace edge on an older Cherokee County home gets its next skunk — or an opossum, which uses the same doors — within a season or two. We trap the residents under the depredation permit for your property, then screen the perimeter with mesh buried at the base, because skunks dig at edges and a surface-fastened screen is a curtain, not a wall. February through April is the season to be brisk about it: that is mating season, when skunks travel furthest, fight under houses, and spray in the encounters — most of the winter calls in Blacksburg are smell calls, and most of them trace to a void that should have been screened the previous fall. If a dog has been sprayed at the same door repeatedly, we will say plainly what is happening there: the skunk's route and the dog's door are the same route, and the screening changes both.

faqs.q: A skunk sprayed right under our Blacksburg bedroom window. Is it living there?
faqs.a: Very likely denning under the porch or in the crawlspace edge nearby — skunks spray where they are cornered or startled, and repeated spray events at one spot usually mean a resident travelling a fixed route past that window. We trap the animal, then screen the void it was using with buried mesh so the address comes off the route permanently. While the trapping runs, keep dogs in at dusk and dawn if you can: most spray events here are dog encounters at the den door, and they stop when the den closes.

faqs.q: How much does skunk removal cost in Blacksburg?
faqs.a: It depends on whether it is one animal or a den with kits, and how much screening the structure needs — a single skunk under a small porch is a compact job; a crawlspace perimeter on an older pier-built home is a larger one. We inspect, quote firmly before trapping starts, and the quote includes the screening that keeps the next skunk out. Removal runs under a depredation permit issued for your property, arranged as part of the job.
